To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) ensembling methods can lead to less well-calibrated models, and that (ii) calibration methods such as Temperature Scaling need to be applied after the averaging process to achieve good performance in the low-data setting.

(1) standard ensembles are not always calibrated; (2) standard ensembles, when used in combination with mixup regularization, are not calibrated; (3) temperature scaling can help to improve the calibration of deep-ensembled models, provided that the temperature scaling is performed after the averaging process, and not before.
deep-ensembling is a powerful tool to increase the accuracy of a model in the low data setting.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interplay between calibration and ensemble methods in the low data setting.
the calibration of deep-ensembled models

the following questions: How do we calibrate extremely over-parametrised models in the low data limit? How do we combine the best of both worlds: the accuracy of ensembles and the calibration of temperature scaling methods?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the combination of ensembling, mixup regularization, and temperature scaling is the best way to calibrate deep neural networks in the low-data setting.
the calibration properties of deep-ensembled models depend on the data augmentation strategy used.
, when data is scarce, the calibration of probabilisitic models is an extremely subtle problem.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in order to obtain the best calibration properties, one should use mixup regularization, deep-ensembled models, and post-hoc calibration methods such as Temperature Scaling, but the calibration of these models relies on a delicate interplay between all of these techniques.
, in the context of low-data problems, ensembling can help to boost accuracy but can hurt calibration, and calibration methods need to be tweaked to work with ensembling.
the calibration of deep-ensembled predictions can be improved by using a slightly modified version of temperature scaling.
The main takeaway from our work is that
calibration methods are not a panacea for over-confidence and that, when data is scarce, the calibration of ensembles needs to be treated with care.
, in the context of deep-ensemble models, the calibration properties of a deep model can be improved by a simple post-hoc procedure.
, when using deep-ensembes, it is crucial to calibrate the individual models and to use a post-processing calibration method after averaging.
